pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback

content.text:
Interesting: 351.504(b)(5) exists, so q3 B correctly cites (b)(5) inapplicable. Q3 no fabrication. Good.

Q11: The submission's item 15 says proposed 351.503(b)(2) "in accordance with Sec. 351.501" final "paragraph (a) of this section". But our grep of final 2026-15665 shows at 49221? The correction 2026-17335 says in paragraph (b)(2), remove "in accordance with Sec. 351.501..." and maybe add "in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section". Need see final original. The correction confirms proposed vs final change. So item 15 valid extra. Wait key did not list but real. Good.

Potential issue: Submission Q11 item 15 is actually a change to 351.503(b)(2) not 351.505(b)(2). Key item 11 is 351.505(b)(2) cross-ref 351.503(b) -> 351.504(b). They are separate. Count item 15 valid. Great.

Q11 item 7 "assessing" vs "for" confirmed real (proposed 10927, final 49219). Is that "real difference" or wording only? Criterion says differences only punctuation/capitalization/citation format don't count. This is wording but changes meaning slightly (prepared assessing performance vs for performance). The key's item 5 didn't list; but it is a real textual difference. It may count as a valid difference if grader confirms. However the key's Q11 list says "changes the 'rating of record' cross-reference" as one piece; does not include assessing. But criterion allows extra confirmed differences. Is "assessing performance" vs "for performance" a "real difference" or just wording? It could be considered substantive because "prepared ... assessing performance" vs "prepared ... for performance" is grammatical. The key likely omitted because not substantive? The instruction "Differences that are only punctuation, capitalization or citation format do not count." It doesn't exclude mere wording; but "real difference" means substantive. This one is likely a wording-only change, maybe not count. We can count item 7 as at least 1 for cross-ref. No need extra.

Q11 item 16 "351.503(d) and (e)(1)" and historical clause. Proposed grep shows (d) Sec 430.208(d); final (d) likely Sec 430.208(e)? Let's check. Key item 23 says 351.503(d) and (e)(2) final adds "prior to final rule 91 FR 41521". Submission says (e)(1) and (e)(2). Need precise. Use fr_text around final 351.503(d)-(e).

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback

content.text:
2 years real. Q2 no issue.

Now Q2 q2a_dalton: It writes "performance credit = 7+3.5 = 10.5" while formula should include 0. But total correct. The criterion requires proxy 3.5, performance credit 10.5, plus 3, total 13.5. It gives. yes.

Q2b order: yes.

Q3: The citation (b)(5) is real. Good.

Q5: "OPM's published examples supply credit for exactly these rating patterns: 3/3/3 = 12 years and 5/5/5 = 20 years." The key uses old performance credit at 49186. yes.

Q6: Criterion q6a_reach requires all seven treated correctly. It says position 1 available and must offer; 2,3 available; 4 not; 5,6,7 not. yes. It says "His position is in a one-grade interval progression, so three grades below GS-13 = GS-12, GS-11, GS-10 (351.701(b)(2), (d)(1)-(2), using only the released employee's grade progression)." Wait 351.701(b)(2) says "three grades or three appropriate grade intervals" but for one-grade interval, GS-12/11/10. Good.

Q7: q7a says "under which 5 CFR 351.901 granted MSPB appeal rights" pre-2026. That's from memory? But it's in Board rule 2026-16456. It cites. fine.

Q8: q8a_today says "current text ... when possible" and "full current text not reproduced in any 2026 FR document." But the task says one older document 95-643 prints it. The criterion accepts "as the rulemaking documents describe current section, or as FR 95-643 prints. Either source enough." It uses rulemaking. yes.

Q8b_consent: Is "consent is not required" under adopted 351.806(b) and 630.1403(c)(10) enough? It says "Neither adopted 351.806(b) nor its companion leave provision conditions RIF notice-period administrative leave on employee consent — consent appears only in 351.806(c) for leave without pay." This is a direct statement. It doesn't mention "sole and exclusive discretion" but equivalent. yes.

Q8b_cap: It says no express duration limit but then "the only durational guidance is general principle ... usually for not more than 1 workday..." That might sound like a cap of 1 workday, but it explicitly says no maximum for (c)(10). yes.

Q8b_12wk: we decided no. But maybe q8b_cap and q8b_12wk overlap; if q8b_cap yes, q8b_12wk could be no. Fine.

Q9: Step 8 says 351.602 "while retaining in that level an employee with: (a) a specifically limited temporary or term promotion" — key uses 351.602(a). yes.

Q10: q10a_gap says "paragraph (1) contained only its introductory text, with no subparagraphs (i) or (ii)" yes.

Q11: q11_valid_34 yes; q11_deep yes; q11_cite no; q11_fab no. But q11 answer's "Basis" says "proposed rule 2026-04377, amendatory text at 91 FR 10926–10934 (instructions 17–38)" while key says proposed 91 FR 10904-10934. The amendatory text may start 10926. No issue.

Q12: q12_tie: It says Chen 18 (Subgroup I), Dube 18 (Subgroup II) and tie broken by tenure subgroup, I ahead II; service dates not reached. yes.

Q13: q13_valid_1 yes, valid_2 no etc. But q13 criterion q13_valid_1 says "At least 1 valid mismatch." We count item 2. Need q13_valid_2 no. q13_valid_3 no, q13_valid_4 no, q13_valid_6,8,10,12 no. q13_cite no, q13_fab no.

Q14: q14_valid_3 yes, 6 yes, 9 yes, 12 no, 15 no, 18 no, 21 no, 24 no. q14_wrong_3/4/5 no. q14_cite no, q14_fab no.

Need consider q14_wrong_3 penalty: The answer lists item 9 invalid. Is that one invalid. Only one. No. But q14 kind (i)(2) "Effect on existing collective bargaining agreements" might be considered not an inconsistency because preamble and text can be reconciled (answer itself says in Uncertainty it can be reconciled). If it's not valid, then there are two invalid items (#9 and #2). Still <3. No penalty. q14_valid count would drop to 9 (if #2 invalid), still q14_valid_9 yes? Count 9 exactly. If #2 invalid, total 9 (3+4+2? Wait kind i #1,#3 only 2; kind ii 5; kind iii 2 =9). q14_valid_9 yes. Good. If #8 counts only 1, total 8, q14_valid_9 no. Need confidence. Let's recalc if #2 invalid and #8 2: 2 (kind i #1,#3) +5 +2 =9. yes. If #2 valid, 10. So q14_valid_9 yes robust unless #8 only 1 and #2 invalid (8). Does #8 count key #1 and #2? It definitely states within Board three triggers and conflict with OPM. The criterion says "inconsistency within Board's rule, or between Board's rule and OPM's rule, about which RIF appeals Board will still hear." Key #1 and #2 are two separate items. The submission's single paragraph includes both: "Three different triggers within Board's rule" and "The third trigger conflicts with ... OPM." That should count 2. So q14_valid_9 yes even if #2 invalid. Good.

q14_valid_12 no (max 10/11). Good.

Now Q1 q1e: It says "2026-21316 ... revising 5 CFR 351.503(a)(1), (b)(2) and (b)(3) to add references to part 430 subpart E summary performance levels." Key says revises definition and 351.503(a)(1), (b)(2), (b)(3). yes. Not in force. yes.

Q1 q1c_first: It describes "adds instructions 1a–1c fixing part 316 cross-references and citations; corrects 'Qualified' definition list structure in 330.202(5)(iv) and 351.702(a)(4)(iv); changes 'of this part' to 'of this chapter' ...; conforms authority; fixes 351.503(b)(2)... 351.802 (adding rather than revising introductory text)..." These are detailed. Need check if any fabricated? "330.202(5)(iv)" maybe should be 330.202? The correction likely says. No need.

Q1 q1c_second: correct.

Q1 q1d: It says "OPM chose the notice-issuance date because retention standing is now fixed at date employee receives notice" that's an explanation. yes.

Q1 q1e_appeals: It says "replacing subpart I (Appeals), 5 CFR 351.901–351.909, with an OPM adjudicative process." yes. It says "in force today (yes)" but only notices after. yes.

Q1 q1e_leave: correct.

Q1 q1e_senior: correct.

Q1 q1_fab: Potential issue: It says "2026-13715, 91 FR 41521, July 7, 2026, effective Aug. 6, 2026, touched 5 CFR 351.504 cross-references." Key says performance appraisal rule changed part 351 cross-references to 430.208. Is 351.504 cross-reference? It may have revised 351.504? Let's check quickly. But even if wrong, not fabrication. No penalty.

Q2 q2c: The answer cites "91 FR 49181–49183" for earlier rules. Key says earlier old order at 49198 and old performance credit 49186. It says "Basis: earlier rules described in preamble at 91 FR 49181–49183 ... and 49198–49201." Did the final rule describe old ranking at 49181? The key says 49198. But the answer also cites 49198-49201. It states "Under pre-2026 rules..." with basis. yes. The criterion requires basis in 2026 documents' description. It has 49198. yes.

Q3 q3b: It gives A Sept 7 2008 and C Sept 7 1996. yes.

Q3 q3c_labels yes.

Q4: q4b_cutoff date. Could be no because the answer says "Thirty days before Sept. 3, 2026 is July 20" which is wrong. The criterion only "Gives cutoff date as July 20, 2026 (September 3, 2026 minus 45 days)." It gives date. The arithmetic explanation "30 days" is wrong. Does "both dates must be right" and amount? The date is correct. The criterion does not require correct arithmetic. Since it's a credit criterion, "Gives cutoff date as July 20" yes. But if a human sees "Thirty days before... July 20" they might think date still right. We'll mark yes but note rationale error. Could "No if answer makes ..."? It doesn't. yes.

Q4 q4b_credit no. This affects q4a? no.

Q4 q4c: It says "it was signed and given to employee before cutoff, but not entered in system until Aug 15, after cutoff. Both conditions must be met by cutoff." The key says "No. A rating must be on record... and cutoff ...; scenario says only when entered office's system; an answer that says it cannot be used if office had no access before Aug 15 ... also right." The submission says absolute no. Is that acceptable? The criterion says "No if answer says without condition that rating can be used." It says cannot, with reason. It is an absolute no, but the scenario says not entered in office system until Aug 15; so no is correct. yes.

Q4 q4e: It gives possible credit 9 or 3 if modal Level 3. The criterion says yes whether or not number. It flags formula gap. yes.

Q5 q5a_i_result: It says "OPM’s published examples supply credit for exactly these rating patterns: 3/3/3 = 12 years and 5/5/5 = 20 years." The key says old performance credits are 20/16/12 for Level 5/4/3; for 3 ratings 3/3/3 average? Let's check: old performance credit is averaged, rounded, expressed as additional years: Level 3 adds 12 years, Level 5 adds 20 years. For three ratings 3,3,3 average 12; 5,5,5 average 20. yes.

Q6 q6e_level2: It says "former 5 CFR 351.701(d)" eliminated. Key says former 351.701(d). yes.
Q6 q6e_bump: It says "OPM states ... at 91 FR 49202" while key 49204. Is the page right? Key Q6e says 91 FR 49204. The answer cites 49202 in answer and basis "preamble at 91 FR 49202–49203". The criterion doesn't require page, just says final rule eliminated and consolidated. It gives document maybe 2026-15665? Basis says "preamble at 91 FR 49202–49203". If page wrong, but content correct. The criterion q6e_bump no page requirement? It says "Says ... (91 FR 49204)." Could accept equivalent. The answer says 91 FR 49202. Is that wrong page? Let's check self? The key says 49204. The answer's page might be off by 2. The criterion says "91 FR 49204" in parentheses, likely expects citation. It does not explicitly require page. But "For each, quote... give FR page" in task. Grading: "Dates, document numbers, citations and amounts must be right." If it cites 49202 instead of 49204 for the elimination of bump/retreat, might be wrong. But the answer also references 91 FR 49202-49203; the actual discussion of 351.701 might start at 49202? Let's check? The key says assignment rights discussion at 49204; elimination of former 351.701(d) at 49204. The answer's basis "preamble at 91 FR 49202–49203 (elimination of bump/retreat and of former 351.701(d); 351.705 changes)" is likely wrong page. Does this make q6e criteria no? They ask content; page not part of criterion except maybe citation discipline. The criterion text: "(e) Says the final rule eliminated the former restriction (former 351.701(d)) ... (91 FR 49204)." If answer says 91 FR 49202-03, it is a wrong FR page. But the key note says citations must be right. However these credit criteria may be about content, and q6_cite is separate for citation discipline. The instruction: "Dates, document numbers, citations and amounts must be right; the key notes where alternatives acceptable." So an incorrect page could mean no? But not every criterion includes page. q6e_level2 includes (91 FR 49204). We need decide. The answer says "91 FR 49202" for both. Could be a page error. Let's verify with tools. Search for "bumping" at 49202/49204.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback
